chapter: Forming the band in New York
title: His status at 'Bama State and self-taught writing
summary: He was part student, part teacher for about a year and a half and learned theory on his own.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x:
I'd like to go back for just one minute to be clear on a couple of points, some specifics.

How long, exactly, did you attend 'Bama State?

I went there in '31.

We left there in '34.
'34. And, you said before that at one point, you were in charge of the department and something. What was your status at the school, and how did that change over that period of time?

Well, I was doing more of that than I was in class. You know?

Well, actually, I didn't get too much out of it because once I left the school, the president wasn't too happy about it, especially after the boys stayed with me. You know?
Right.
So, a lot of things that I wanted to get for my critics and things
You never received them. And, but you were part student and part teacher?
Right.
So, you had sort of a double function there?
Right.
So, you were teaching there and going to school?
That's just about a year and a half, or something like that. Two.
About a year and a half, you were doing that.
Yeah, before I was doing that. That's after the regular teacher left.
Right. Okay. And, you took private music lessons at that time too?
Private? No. I didn't get into private music after that. I didn't get a chance.
Well, who were you
You're talking about music lessons.
Yes.
No. I didn't. I had, oh, this fellow's name was—I don't know if I did before he left. Maybe I can get that name for you a little later.
Okay. But, you were studying trumpet?
Right.
Were you studying?
I was in trumpet.
You were?
Trumpet.
And, were you studying theory or any of that at this point? Or, were you doing it all on your own?
I was doing it mostly on my own.
Mostly on your own. So, you, those were things you sort of drew together yourself? I mean, through practical
experience.
That's right.
In working for your band, and arranging and composing that way rather than formal study with other people.
That's right. I had mostly self.
And also, you were able to pass this on to Sammy Lowe and Avery Parrish and some of the others.
That's what I did.
